questions.text: What is the minimum total length of a 180° hook on a 25 mm diameter bar, measured from the tip of one end to the tip of the other end?

rationale.a: 150 mm is the absolute minimum for hook length (some codes use this as a minimum cap), but 12db = 300 mm for 25 mm bar.
rationale.b: 200 mm is too short for a 25 mm bar.
rationale.correct: For a 25 mm bar (NSCP 7.1.1), the 180° hook total length is approximately 12db. So: 12 × 25 = 300 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: What is the minimum extension length from the inside of the bend for a 90° stirrup hook with 16 mm diameter ties?

rationale.a: 64 mm = 4db, which is the inside bend diameter (not extension) for ≤16 mm stirrups.
rationale.c: 192 mm = 12db, which is the extension for 90° longitudinal hooks, not stirrup hooks.
rationale.d: 128 mm = 8db, which applies to 28 mm bars, not 16 mm ties.
rationale.correct: For 90° stirrup hooks with ties ≤16 mm, the extension length is 6db (NSCP 7.1.1). For 16 mm ties: 6 × 16 = 96 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: For stirrup ties of 25 mm diameter with 90° hooks, what is the minimum inside bend diameter (db)?

rationale.a: 100 mm = 4db, which applies to stirrups ≤16 mm, not 20–25 mm.
rationale.c: 200 mm = 8db, which applies to longitudinal bars 28 mm and 32 mm.
rationale.d: 250 mm = 10db, which applies to 36 mm longitudinal bars.
rationale.correct: For 90° stirrup hooks with ties 20–25 mm, the minimum inside diameter is 6db (NSCP 7.1.2). For a 25 mm tie: 6 × 25 = 150 mm. Larger stirrups require wider bends.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A 180° hook on a 16 mm diameter bar has a minimum extension length of __db. What is this value?

rationale.a: 2db is not a standard value in NSCP.
rationale.c: 6db is the extension for stirrup hooks ≤16 mm or seismic hooks.
rationale.d: 8db applies to 180° hooks with extensions on both sides (2 × 4db).
rationale.correct: The extension length (measured from inside of bend to end of bar) for 180° hooks is 4db, regardless of bar size (NSCP 7.1.1). For a 16 mm bar: 4 × 16 = 64 mm. The extension on one side is 4db; since a 180° hook has extensions on both sides, total extension = 8db.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A 180° standard hook is formed on a 20 mm diameter bar. What is the minimum inside bend diameter (db) required?

rationale.b: 120 mm = 6db, which is for 90° longitudinal hooks or stirrups ≥20 mm, not 180° hooks.
rationale.c: 240 mm = 12db, which is for 90° longitudinal hooks (inside diameter), not 180° hooks.
rationale.d: 160 mm = 8db, which applies to 28 mm and 32 mm bars, not 20 mm.
rationale.correct: For 180° hooks on 20 mm bars (Grade 50/60), the minimum inside diameter is 6db (NSCP 2015 §425.3.1 Table 425-3.1). For a 20 mm bar: 6 × 20 = 120 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A 36 mm diameter longitudinal bar requires a 90° hook at the end. What is the minimum inside bend diameter (db)?

rationale.a: 144 mm = 4db, which applies to 180° hooks or small bars, not large 36 mm bars.
rationale.b: 216 mm = 6db, which applies to bars up to 25 mm, not 36 mm.
rationale.d: 288 mm = 8db, which applies to 28 mm and 32 mm bars, not 36 mm.
rationale.correct: For 36 mm bars (#11), the minimum inside bend diameter for 90° hook is 8db (NSCP 2015 §425.3.1 Table 425-3.1). For a 36 mm bar: 8 × 36 = 288 mm. Larger bars require wider bends to prevent concrete crushing.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: In seismic column design for an SMRF (Special Moment Resisting Frame), the confinement hoops require a seismic hook. What is the required bend angle and minimum extension length?

options.text: 90° bend, 4db extension, typically used in non-seismic zones where lateral forces are minimal
180° bend, 8db extension, often specified for extreme seismic conditions to ensure maximum confinement
90° bend, 12db extension, which is generally applied in high-rise buildings to accommodate additional load

rationale.a: 90° bend is standard for non-seismic stirrups, not seismic columns (ERR-STRC-014).
rationale.c: 180° bend is for longitudinal bar anchorage, not stirrup/hoop confinement.
rationale.d: 12db extension applies to longitudinal 90° hooks, not seismic hoops.
rationale.correct: Seismic hoops in SMRF columns require 135° bend angle with 6db extension, with an absolute minimum of 75 mm (NSCP 12.13.5, ACI 318-19 § 18.6). This ensures tight, closed confinement and prevents bar buckling.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A designer uses 90° hooks for column confinement hoops in a seismic frame. Is this correct per NSCP seismic provisions, and what should it be?

options.text: Yes, 90° is correct, as long as additional reinforcement is provided to compensate for the reduced hook angle
No; seismic hoops must use 135° hooks (ERR-STRC-014).
90° is acceptable if the extension is increased to 12db, provided that the overall structural integrity is not compromised
No; seismic hoops must use 180° hooks, ensuring maximum confinement and structural resilience during seismic events

rationale.a: 90° hooks are standard for non-seismic stirrups, not seismic confinement.
rationale.c: Increasing extension to 12db does not make 90° hooks compliant for seismic design.
rationale.d: 180° hooks are for longitudinal bar anchorage, not stirrups.
rationale.correct: Seismic column confinement hoops in SMRF frames must use 135° bend angle, not 90° (NSCP 12.13.5). This error (ERR-STRC-014) is one of the most common seismic mistakes. The 135° hook closes the loop more tightly and prevents bar buckling.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: An engineer specifies a 180° hook on a 20 mm bar with 40 mm extension length and 4db inside diameter. Is this hook compliant with NSCP minimum requirements?

options.text: Yes, compliant, as it meets the basic criteria for hook specifications
No; extension is too short (minimum 4db = 80 mm required).
Yes, but hook can be simplified to 90°, which may reduce material usage
No; inside diameter is too large (minimum 2db = 40 mm), which can affect structural integrity

rationale.a: The hook violates the extension requirement.
rationale.c: The hook is non-compliant due to insufficient extension; it cannot be simplified without meeting all requirements.
rationale.d: Inside diameter 4db = 80 mm is correct; the problem is extension, not diameter.
rationale.correct: The 180° hook requires 4db inside diameter (4 × 20 = 80 mm, compliant) and 4db extension (4 × 20 = 80 mm minimum required). The specified 40 mm extension is only half the code requirement. Hook is non-compliant; extension must be at least 80 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Compare the inside bend diameter requirements: a 90° longitudinal hook on a 20 mm bar vs. a 90° stirrup hook on a 20 mm tie.

options.text: Both require 6db, ensuring consistency in bending requirements across different hook types
Longitudinal 6db; Stirrup 4db, which is standard for smaller diameter ties
Longitudinal 4db; Stirrup 6db, reflecting the different stress conditions in ties

rationale.d: Stirrup is 6db (20 mm = ≥20 mm tier), not 4db (which is ≤16 mm tier).
rationale.correct: 90° longitudinal hooks have inside bend diameter 6db, but extension length beyond bend is 12db (NSCP 2015 §425.3.1). 90° stirrup hooks on 20 mm ties have 6db (NSCP 7.1.2, tier: 20–25 mm). For a 20 mm bar: longitudinal = 240 mm, stirrup = 120 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.
